description: A 31-band vocoder with a slider for the attack, release, level and pan of each band: the modulator's band envelopes amplitude-modulate the carrier's bands, and a 31 by 31 grid sets which drives which.

params.text: Takes the vocoder out of circuit and sends the carrier input to Out-L and the modulator input to Out-R, each through its gain knob; the lamp is red while it is on.
Steps to the next of six preset couplings, numbered 0 to 5, replacing whatever the matrix held and setting the shift count to zero; 4 is one-to-one, 5 is its reverse, and 0 to 3 are logarithmic.
Stops the Shift L and Shift R inputs from moving the matrix; leaving the two step buttons working; the lamp blinks while it is on.
Moves every connection in the matrix one column to the right, wrapping round at the end, and adds one to the shift count.
Moves every connection in the matrix one column to the left, wrapping round at the end, and takes one off the shift count.
Multiplies the carrier input by 0.1 to 10 before it is split into bands, despite the panel label reading Mod Gain.
Multiplies the modulator input by 0.1 to 10 before it is split into bands, despite the panel label reading Carr Gain.
Takes that modulator band out of the vocoder; the lamp is lit while the band is in. Right-clicking mutes every other band instead, and right-clicking again undoes that.
Connects one modulator band to one carrier band, so that band's envelope sets the carrier band's level; the lamp is lit while connected. Right-click two in turn to fill the line between them.
Sets how fast the envelope follower for that modulator band rises, in seconds; each band has its own range, the low bands reaching far longer times than the high ones.
Sets how fast the envelope follower for that modulator band falls, in seconds; each band has its own range, the low bands reaching far longer times than the high ones.
Amplifies that modulator band's contribution, in dB; the bottom of the travel is a small positive gain, so the slider cannot silence a band.
Places that carrier band between the two outputs by a constant-power law: the bottom of the travel puts it in Out-L alone, the top in Out-R alone, and the middle splits it evenly.
Moves the even-numbered bands one step toward Out-L and the odd-numbered ones one step toward Out-R, so the spread across the pair widens.
Moves the even-numbered bands one step toward Out-R and the odd-numbered ones one step toward Out-L, so the spread across the pair narrows.
Sets every pan slider to the middle, splitting every band evenly between the two outputs.
Moves every pan slider one step up, which sends every band further toward Out-R, despite the maker's README calling this the button that pans to the left.
Moves every pan slider one step down, which sends every band further toward Out-L, despite the maker's README calling this the button that pans to the right.
Moves every level slider one step up, amplifying every band.
Moves every level slider one step down, attenuating every band.
Moves every attack slider one step up, lengthening the rise of every band's envelope follower.
Moves every attack slider one step down, shortening the rise of every band's envelope follower.
Moves every release slider one step up, lengthening the fall of every band's envelope follower.
Moves every release slider one step down, shortening the fall of every band's envelope follower.

inputs.text: The signal that is split into 31 third-octave bands and amplitude-modulated by the modulator's band envelopes; one channel only.
The signal that is split into 31 third-octave bands, each band's envelope setting the level of the carrier band it is connected to; one channel only.
A rise past 0.1V moves every connection in the matrix one column to the right, wrapping round at the end; it is ignored while Hold or ByPass is on.
A rise past 0.1V moves every connection in the matrix one column to the left, wrapping round at the end; it is ignored while Hold or ByPass is on.

outputs.text: The sum of every modulated carrier band as the pan sliders weight it for this channel; a band whose pan slider is at the bottom of its travel reaches only this jack.
The sum of every modulated carrier band as the pan sliders weight it for this channel; a band whose pan slider is at the top of its travel reaches only this jack.

notes: the filter bank is worked out once for a sample rate of 44100Hz and never recomputed, so at any other rate the 31 bands do not land on the frequencies they are named after.
the module starts in matrix mode 4, a one-to-one coupling, so a carrier and a modulator patched in are enough to hear it.
the two seven-segment readouts carry the matrix mode number and the number of columns the matrix has been shifted; they are drawings and cannot be clicked.
the carrier and the modulator each have to be one channel. For a stereo signal, use one vocoder per side.
the module has no menu of its own; what a patch stores is the bypass state, the matrix mode, the shift count, the hold setting, every matrix connection and every mute.
the level sliders come up well above unity, scaled band by band to an equal-loudness curve, so the module is loud before anything is touched.
